_README:
Rulings that DISAGREE with what every scraped source spells, applied LAST by the builder -- after the overlay, the insert-set split and the self-naming filter, all of which are entitled to run on the source's own words first. See loadOverrides()/applyOverride() in build-parallel-vocabulary.cjs for the mechanism and why the additive overlay (checklist-parallel-overlays.json) cannot do this: its merge rule lets the SOURCE win once one exists, which is backwards for a ruling that overrides an EXISTING source spelling.

Each entry is scoped to an exact (sport, year, setKey). `drop` removes names case-insensitively even though a source stated them; `add` is the ruling's own spelling, appended only if not already present after the drop. Re-applying is idempotent. Every entry that adds a name MUST carry non-empty `ruling`, `rulingDate` and `reason` -- loadOverrides() fails the build otherwise (assertOverrideEntry).

overrides.ruling: Drew, 2026-09-25 -- the unnumbered non-auto Super Box exclusive rung is spelled "Silver Crackle Foil", matching the spelling PR #2427 folds the 2026 catalog onto. A corpus that adopts sales onto "Foilboard" (or a boilerplate-suffixed/parenthetical variant) would fight that fold in the 03:00Z nightly.

Only baseball|2026|topps-series-1 has a scraped source today (C:/tmp/ci/csv2/2026-topps-series-1-baseball.csv, not committed to the repo, spelling "Silver Crackle Foil (Super Box exclusive)" on every base row); the other three setKeys carry no crackle rung yet -- this entry is a standing guard, not a correction of an existing row.

overrides.ruling: N/A -- not a spelling ruling. This entry restores the registration PR #2355 (feat(catalog): register 85 named insert/auto keys unblocking Wave-1 Prizm FB/BK + Select BK) already made: `panini-prizm-fireworks` (slug of the bare root "Fireworks") is the registered key insertSetTitleReader.ts / productSetKeys.ts expect. It is a rootRename, not a drop/add, and rootRename has the same non-empty-provenance requirement as add.
overrides.reason: A fuller/different 2024-25 Panini Prizm Basketball CSV spells the Fireworks insert's colour rungs verbatim "Fireworks Prizms Black/Gold/..." (confirmed against the raw source -- "Prizms" really is in the checklist's own text, not builder noise). Each colour landed as its OWN one-item root ("Fireworks Prizms Black", "Fireworks Prizms Gold", ... -- 9 roots, never merged, because no bare "Fireworks Prizms" child exists to anchor the merge). insertSetTitleReader.ts looks up `${setKey}-${slugifyRoot(root)}` per root, so every one of those 9 slugs (`panini-prizm-fireworks-prizms-black`, etc.) misses #2355's single registered `panini-prizm-fireworks` -- and the terse title "...Fireworks Some Player #6" (which named no colour) stopped resolving at all, breaking tests/insertSetF4BaseConfirmedUntouched.test.ts's #2355 pin. Renaming all 9 roots' LABEL to "Fireworks" (never touching any child's real, fully-spelled name) lets the terse title match the shared root and the fully-spelled titles keep matching their own child, both under the one key #2355 registered.

overrides.reason: C:/tmp/ci/csv2/2024-panini-zenith-football.csv states "Z Marquee"'s colours on SIBLING categories (insert-z-marquee-blue/gold/orange/red/white, each blank on the bare insert-z-marquee row) -- the shape insertSetsFromCategories() is built to read. backend/data/checklists/scraped/acq-2026-09-19-beckett-panini-zenith-fb/2024-panini-zenith-football.csv (committed 09-19, added to this rebuild's --dirs) states the SAME colours directly on the bare insert-z-marquee category's own rows instead. categoryRowsByProduct merges both files' rows for this one product, so the merged 'insert-z-marquee' category is no longer blank on every row, and insertSetsFromCategories's own precondition (its whole point: a bare category that states no parallel of its own) correctly, structurally refuses to fire -- 'Z Marquee' silently vanished from the corpus, taking 5 colour children with it, and breaking insertSetTitleReader.test.ts's own 'coverage gap has closed' pin. Both sources agree on the card; only the merge of their two different shapes produced the gap.

TOKEN LEAK (2026-09-25) -- see build-parallel-vocabulary.cjs's applyDropInsertSetRoots header. This rebuild's fuller CSV set (vs the 09-19 build) added real, checklist-backed error-variation rows whose text literally embeds a player's first name ("ERR Photo Actuall Is Juan Eichelberger", "UER Photo Is Joe Pittman", "UER Middle Name Is Nolan"). playerSegmentIsAPerson.ts's everyCorpusName reads these into the SAME shared token vocabulary titleNamesFinish/cardQueryParser/computeHobbyIqCardId all consult; once "Juan"/"Joe"/"Nolan" recur across >=2 base brands (this row plus a player-named insert on a different product -- "Nolan" pairs with baseball|2003|topps's "Record Breakers Nolan Ryan"), that module's own frequency floor (documented in its header as the exact defence against this) admits them, and every OTHER "Juan ..."/"Joe ..."/"Nolan ..." sale in the pool loses its first name. Dropped, not corrected -- these are real cards; the corpus simply does not need to spell-adopt or vocabulary-index a one-off error-variation name.

overrides.reason: NOT A BASE-LADDER RUNG (2026-09-25). A newly-included fuller CSV (data/checklists/scraped/acq-2026-09-19-beckett-panini-donruss-fb-full/2024-panini-donruss-football.csv) carries a bare "Purple" parallel column value ONLY under three AUTOGRAPH insert categories (auto-rated-rookies-autographs, auto-signature-marks, auto-signature-series -- verified against the raw source, isAuto=true, printRun 150 on every row). The builder's base-wins guard in splitInsertSets treats any `auto-*` category as base-like (readChecklistCategory's kind==='auto'), which is right for `auto-base*` (the base card, signed) but wrong here: this product's BASE ladder's own purple rung is separately and distinctly named "Purple Press Proof" (confirmed present under the plain `base` category on the same CSV) -- bare "Purple" is the autograph inserts' OWN colour, never a rung of the base card. tests/r31R33WriteGuards.test.ts pins "purple" as refused for panini-donruss alongside other insert-only fragments (passing grade, downtown duo, ...); this bare "Purple" is exactly that shape, not a base parallel. Dropped from parallels[] only -- "Purple Press Proof" (the real base rung) is untouched, and nothing about the autograph inserts' own child rows is affected (they are not present as insert-set entries in this corpus shape, since their parallel column states only the bare colour word, same as the base-wins guard already handles for other products).

TOKEN LEAK, a THIRD reader affected (2026-09-25) -- see build-parallel-vocabulary.cjs's applyDropInsertSetRoots header for the mechanism (that header documents playerSegmentIsAPerson.ts; this is the SAME class of defect in a DIFFERENT consumer, statedFinishFromChecklist.ts, which builds its own GLOBAL finish-word vocabulary from every corpus name). "Chicago Collection" is a real Donruss insert set this rebuild's fuller CSV set surfaced for the first time; its token "chicago" entered the global finish-word stream and made every OTHER title naming a Chicago sports team ("...Chicago Bears...") read as stating an unconfirmed finish -- measured directly: tests/r32SplitScopeR55.test.ts's 86-row fixture gained a false park on a Caleb Williams / Chicago Bears row for exactly this reason. Dropped, not corrected -- "Chicago Collection" remains a real, checklist-backed insert; only its contribution to the global vocabulary is removed.

TOKEN LEAK (2026-09-25) -- see the 2002 Donruss entry above for the full mechanism. "Chicago Collection" recurs here, the second of the two occurrences that gave the global "chicago" token its foothold.

TOKEN LEAK, a FOURTH reader affected (2026-09-25) -- see build-parallel-vocabulary.cjs's applyDropInsertSetRoots header for the general mechanism. "The Ryan Express" (Nolan Ryan's nickname) is a real, checklist-backed image-variation insert this rebuild's fuller CSV set surfaced for the first time; its token "ryan" combined with baseball|2003|topps's pre-existing "Record Breakers Nolan Ryan" (already on main, previously a harmless single occurrence) crosses persistVendorSalesToPool.service.ts's / cardQueryParser.js's shared player-name-guess vocabulary's corpus-frequency floor for the first time -- measured directly: tests/tcaEbayPlayerNameChecklistRecovery.test.ts's Upper Deck hockey fixture lost "Ryan" from three unrelated titles (Ryan Strome, Ryan Greene, Ryan Suzuki). Dropped, not corrected -- "The Ryan Express" remains a real, checklist-backed insert; only its contribution to the shared vocabulary is removed. baseball|2003|topps's own "Record Breakers Nolan Ryan" is untouched (it alone, at one occurrence, was never the problem).
